source: 2022 LiDAR canopy height and cover (Sunshine Coast LiDAR, ELVIS), computed by the map, 24 Oct 2026

classes.label: Open ground: grass, gardens, bare (under 2 m)
classes.note: Pasture, lawn, gardens, tracks, recent clearing. Sun all day; the easiest ground to plant into.

classes.label: Shrubs and young regrowth (2-5 m)
classes.note: Lantana, wattle and young regrowth. Often the first place to work: clear weeds, keep the natives, plant into the gaps.

classes.label: Low or young forest (5-15 m)
classes.note: Regrowth and young forest. Good shelter belts and edges; thin selectively for light.

classes.label: Mid forest (15-25 m)
classes.note: Established forest. Shade-tolerant understorey, bush food, habitat; the canopy closes over most plantings.

classes.label: Tall forest (25-35 m)
classes.note: Mature eucalypt forest. Keep buildings, tanks and tracks out of falling distance of the big trees.

classes.label: Very tall forest (over 35 m)
classes.note: Emergent giants: the oldest, most valuable habitat trees on the block.

classes.label: Gaps in the forest canopy
classes.note: Places inside the forest where the canopy opens up (less than three-quarters cover): light wells for planting, or recent tree fall.
